excludedAttempts.reason: Python inference GPU activity was observed around an earlier prose window; both original prose attempts and an incomplete medium-prose attempt were excluded conservatively.

limitations: Two local prompts, not the complete selected SPEED-Bench launch suite.
Same source weights and exact prompt token IDs; engines can produce different greedy continuations.
Mere output hashes cover its separated reasoning and visible response; Splash hashes cover raw completion text, so cross-engine hash equality is not asserted.
Shared workstation, normal memory pressure and monitored GPU activity; GPU clock frequency is not fixed.
The main code runs used the original known-process monitor; reverse code controls and prose runs also monitor Python/other compute GPU clients.
Owned Splash server stayed resident during mere.run and its GPU counters had to remain unchanged.
Synchronized profiles change scheduling and are excluded from throughput tables.

provenance.dataCollection: One active GPU workload; owned Splash server remains resident but its GPU counters must stay unchanged during mere.run.

prompts.code: Write a complete Python implementation of an LRU cache using a dictionary and a doubly linked list, with get and put operations, type hints, and a short usage example. Return the code directly without introductory prose.
prompts.prose: Explain how a small community could turn an abandoned railway station into a public library. Discuss the building, accessibility, staffing, the collection, and a realistic opening-day scene. Write approximately 400 words of clear, connected prose.
